methods.name: writeTo
methods.description:
Write log events to a sink.

Sinks are processed in configuration order, receiving events after all preceding stages have been applied.

Example :
               Evaluated at runtime for each log event batch
               Return true to write to sink, false to skip
Example :
let consoleEnabled = true;
___COMPODOC_EMPTY_LINE___
const logger = new LoggerConfiguration()
  .writeTo(new ConsoleSink(), () => consoleEnabled)
  .create();
___COMPODOC_EMPTY_LINE___
// Later: disable console logging
consoleEnabled = false;

jsdoctags.comment: • Optional function that controls whether the sink is active Evaluated at runtime for each log event batch Return true to write to sink, false to skip

Example :
let consoleEnabled = true;

const logger = new LoggerConfiguration()
  .writeTo(new ConsoleSink(), () => consoleEnabled)
  .create();

// Later: disable console logging
consoleEnabled = false;

functions.name: configureGlobalLogger
functions.description: Configure the global logger instance. This should be called once at application startup. All packages using

jsdoctags.comment:
Example :
import { configureGlobalLogger } from '@cocoar/logging';

configureGlobalLogger((config) =>
config
.minLevel('debug')
.writeTo(new ConsoleSink({ includeProperties: true }))
);

functions.name: getLogger
functions.description: Get the global logger instance. If not configured, returns a default logger with console sink.

jsdoctags.comment: • Optional source context (component name, class name, etc.)
Logger instance, optionally enriched with source context

Example :
import { getLogger } from '@cocoar/logging';

const logger = getLogger('MyComponent');
logger.info('Component initialized');

functions.name: resetGlobalLogger
functions.description: Reset the global logger (mainly for testing purposes). ⚠️ Use with caution - this affects all packages using the logger.
